Ausangate Mountain: the sacred jewel of the Andes

The Ausangate is one of the most breathtaking mountains in Peru and a sacred peak for Andean communities. Rising above 6,300 meters (20,669 ft), it’s perfect for travelers seeking multi-day trekking adventures surrounded by glaciers, colorful lagoons, and native wildlife.

Why visit Ausangate?

  • Remote high-altitude landscapes
  • Authentic Andean culture
  • Ideal for adventure trekking

Location: Vilcanota Mountain Range, Cusco
⏱ Recommended duration: 2 to 5 days

Best for adventurous travelers and trekking lovers.

Seven Lakes of Ausangate: a hidden natural wonder

Located at the base of Ausangate, the Seven Lakes of Ausangate offer a more accessible yet equally stunning experience. Each lake displays a different color—turquoise, green, deep blue—creating a truly unique natural spectacle.

Highlights of this experience:

  • One-day hike from Pacchanta
  • Relaxing hot springs after the trek
  • Stunning views of Ausangate

Starting point: Pacchanta
⏱ Duration: Full day

Perfect if you want a high-altitude experience without a long trek.

Rainbow Mountain: Cusco’s iconic landscape

The famous Montaña de Colores, also known as Vinicunca, is one of Cusco’s most visited attractions. Its mineral-rich layers create vibrant natural colors unlike anywhere else in the world.

Why include it in your trip?

  • One of Peru’s most photographed destinations
  • Short but challenging hike due to altitude
  • Ideal for full-day tours from Cusco

Altitude: 5,200 m (17,060 ft)
⏱ Duration: Full day

Proper acclimatization in Cusco is essential.
